title: Wall-Clock Last-Write-Wins versus Happens-Before
objective: Add two merge policies to the replicated store — last-write-wins by wall clock, and version-vector / happens-before detection — and produce a script that loses a concurrent write under LWW and then flags the same pair as concurrent under the vector policy.
whyThisMatters: Once you have replication and fencing, the remaining lie is that time itself is a total order. The SWE curriculum never forces a lost update that exists only because two clocks disagreed. If you cannot make that loss appear, you will keep treating 'latest' as a fact instead of a policy.
evidence: Git history showing LWW committed before version vectors, not a single drop of both policies
A reproduction script and captured run: LWW discards one concurrent write; the vector policy reports the pair as concurrent and retains both values or a conflict record
README defining happens-before for this store, with the two writes labeled concurrent rather than ordered
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The LWW reproduction injects a clock skew (or an assigned timestamp) so the physically earlier write carries the later timestamp, and the captured run shows that write winning and the other value gone.
The vector-clock (or version-vector) reproduction uses the same two writes and reports them as concurrent; both values or an explicit conflict record remain inspectable after merge.
README states a happens-before rule in terms of replica ids and counters (or equivalent), and names the two writes as concurrent under that rule.
Wall-clock timestamps are not used as the sole merge key in the vector policy.
